```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

zuroar gives R compressed sets of whole numbers from 0 to 2^32 - 1, or to
2^64 - 1 with the 64-bit class. Dense stretches and long runs take a
fraction of the memory of a plain vector, and membership, counts and set
operations work without expanding them. Bitmaps are written in the
portable Roaring format that Python, Java, Go and Rust programs share.

```{r setup}
library(zuroar)
```

## Build a bitmap

`roar()` takes whole numbers in any order, with or without duplicates.
`roar_range()` takes both ends of a range, included as in `seq()`, and
`roar_add()` and `roar_remove()` return a changed copy.

```{r}
x <- roar(c(1L, 5L, 9L, 100000L))
x <- roar_add(x, 7L)
x <- roar_remove(x, 5L)
y <- roar_range(1, 1e6)
y <- roar_remove(y, from = 10, to = 19)
```

## Use it like a sorted vector

A bitmap behaves like `sort(unique(v))`: `length()` counts its values,
positions start at 1, `[` returns a bitmap and `[[` a single value.
`c()` is the union, and adding a number shifts every value.

```{r}
length(x)
x[[2]]
x[2:3]
head(y, 3)
c(x, roar(42L)) + 10
```

## Ask questions

`roar_contains()` is the fast membership test. Ranges are inclusive,
`roar_rank()` counts the values at or below one, `roar_select()` finds
the `k`-th smallest, and `roar_next()` the nearest value above.

```{r}
roar_contains(x, c(5L, 6L))
roar_count(y, from = 10, to = 20)
roar_rank(x, 9L)
roar_select(x, c(1, 2))
roar_next(x, 8L)
```

## Combine sets

Between bitmaps, `|` is the union, `&` the intersection and `<=` a
subset test. Counts and similarities need no intermediate bitmap.

```{r}
x | y
x & y
x <= y
roar_cardinality(x, y, op = "and")
roar_jaccard(x, y)
```

## Save and share

A bitmap survives `saveRDS()` and `readRDS()` like any R object, stored
compressed:

```{r}
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(y, path)
readRDS(path) == y
```

`roar_serialize()` writes the portable Roaring format as a raw vector,
for other programs and other Roaring libraries, and `roar_unserialize()`
checks bytes before reading them.

```{r}
b <- roar_serialize(x)
x2 <- roar_unserialize(b)
x2 == x
```

Bitmaps are sent to and from `mirai` workers like any other value. The
64-bit class, `roar64()`, needs `roar_serial_config()` for that; the
32-bit one works with or without it.

```{r, include = FALSE}
# A daemon is a fresh R process: hand it this session's library paths, so
# it finds the zuroar being documented.
Sys.setenv(R_LIBS = paste(.libPaths(), collapse = .Platform$path.sep))
```

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("mirai", quietly = TRUE)}
mirai::daemons(1)
m <- mirai::mirai(zuroar::roar_add(x, 8), x = x)
mirai::call_mirai(m)$data
mirai::daemons(0)
```
